title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): S is a scheme, M a locally constant sheaf of finitely generated abelian groups on S, and G the associated finite flat group scheme of multiplicative type (the Cartier dual of M). Its co-Lie complex is ℓ_G ≅ M ⊗^L_Z O_S, with H^0 = ω_G = M⊗O_S and H^{-1} = n_G = Tor_1^Z(M,O_S). Like any two-term complex, it has a k-invariant (extension class) ξ ∈ Ext^2_{O_S}(ω_G, n_G). Given a ring Λ with Λ → O_S, ξ comes from ξ_Λ ∈ Ext^2_Λ(M⊗Λ, Tor_1(M,Λ)). For Λ = Z/n and M locally free over Λ, both M⊗Λ and Tor_1(M,Λ) = _nM are isomorphic to M. So ξ_Λ ∈ H^2(S, End M), and ξ ∈ H^2(S, End E) with E = M⊗_Λ O_S is the image of ξ_Λ under H^2(S, End M) → H^2(S, End M ⊗_Λ O_S) ≅ H^2(S, End E).

On this page: suppose M is trivialised by a Galois étale cover S'→S with group π, so M comes from a π-module M_0, flat over Λ. Then ξ_Λ is the pullback of a class ξ_0 ∈ H^2(B_π, End M_0) = H^2(π, End M_0). By functoriality in π, it suffices to compute the universal case M_0 = (Z/n)^d, π = GL(d, Z/n).

Grothendieck cites Illusie: ξ_0 is the obstruction to lifting the representation of π on M_0 to a representation on a free Z/p^2 module (for n = p). That is, it is the class in H^2(π, M_d(F_p)) of the pullback of the extension 1 → M_d(F_p) → GL_d(Z/p^2) → GL_d(F_p) → 1. For d ≤ 1 the class vanishes (Teichmüller lift of F_p^*). He conjectures it is nonzero for d ≥ 2 in the universal case π = GL(d, F_p).

Finally: if S' is the universal cover (π_1(S) = π finite), the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence gives injectivity of H^2(π, −) → H^2(S, −) on modules trivialised by S', since H^1 of a simply connected S' with finite constant coefficients vanishes. Hence ξ_Λ ≠ 0 in H^2(S, End M).

Purpose: to produce multiplicative finite group schemes (in char p) whose co-Lie complex is not split, i.e. is not determined by ω_G and n_G. This bears on the Dieudonné/crystal theory of finite flat groups that the 'Cristaux' notes study.
errors: The conjecture 'sans doute pas nulle si d ≥ 2' has small exceptions. For p=2, d=2, GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 lifts to GL_2(Z/4) via the integral reflection representation of the A_2 root lattice, so ξ_0 = 0. Splitting of GL_d(Z/p^2) → GL_d(F_p) is also known in some other small cases (e.g. p=3, d=2 by known results on SL_2(Z/9)). Non-splitting holds for p ≥ 5 and all d ≥ 2, and generally outside small (p,d).

Gap: the final step only gives ξ_Λ ≠ 0 in H^2(S, End M). The class relevant to G is ξ ∈ H^2(S, End E), the image under base change to O_S, which may well be killed. The page does not address the non-vanishing of ξ itself.
The injectivity H^2(π, −) → H^2(S, −) requires π_1(S) = π (finite universal cover), as stated. If π were only a finite quotient of a larger π_1, inflation to π_1 could kill ξ_0.

ideas.what: The co-Lie complex of a multiplicative finite group scheme is M ⊗^L O_S, and its k-invariant in Ext^2(ω_G, n_G) descends to H^2(π, End M_0) via the classifying topos B_π.
ideas.modern_name: co-Lie complex ℓ_G and its Postnikov/k-invariant; Hochschild–Serre descent
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (Complexe cotangent et déformations II, 1972), with Grothendieck's 1970 crystalline Dieudonné program
ideas.where_published: Closest is Grothendieck, Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (1974, Montréal lectures); Illusie CC II ch. VII

ideas.what: The k-invariant of M ⊗^L_Z F_p over F_p[π] equals the obstruction to lifting the representation to a free Z/p^2-module.
ideas.modern_name: obstruction to deforming flat modules (Ext^2(M, M⊗I)); Bockstein-type class of GL_d(Z/p^2) → GL_d(F_p)
ideas.where_published: Illusie, Complexe cotangent et déformations I, ch. IV

ideas.what: Non-splitting of GL_d(Z/p^2) → GL_d(F_p) for d ≥ 2 (rank ≤ 1 splits via Teichmüller).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sah (1974) and later authors on splitting of GL_n(Z/p^2) → GL_n(F_p)

ideas.what: Injectivity of H^2(π_1, F) → H^2_et(S, F) when the universal cover is finite.

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes constructing, over a base S whose finite fundamental group maps onto GL_d(F_p), a multiplicative finite flat group scheme killed by p whose co-Lie complex has a nonzero k-invariant over Z/p, obtained from non-splitting of GL_d(Z/p^2) → GL_d(F_p). The final step, non-vanishing of ξ after base change to O_S, is left open.
missed.quote: on trouvera un élément non nul ξ_Λ ∈ H²(S, End(M))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a concrete mechanism (a group-theoretic Bockstein) for non-decomposability of co-Lie complexes of finite flat group schemes, relevant to crystalline Dieudonné theory. I am unsure whether this precise example is recorded in Illusie CC II or later work.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a nice, mostly correct sketch linking the co-Lie complex's k-invariant to the non-splitting of GL_d(Z/p^2) → GL_d(F_p), but it explicitly relies on Illusie and is essentially routine given his theory. The conjecture also has small-case exceptions.
transcription_corrections: 'sous les conditions de 1.5[?]' likely reads '§1.5' or 'n°1.5'; 'M_0 étant [?] supposé' is probably 'M_0 étant aussi supposé' or similar.
'Lorsque n=p (premier)' is an interlinear insertion qualifying the following sentence (and the Z/p^2Z lifting statement).
In the last paragraph 'injectif' appears underlined or struck; the reading 'est injectif' is consistent with the Hochschild–Serre argument.
